questions.question: Which color is best to wear so others can see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding a motorcycle. Bright clothing makes you easier to see at any time of day.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Let the front tire lock up.
Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and evenly to stop safely and quickly. Do not let either tire skid.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be a:
questions.explanation: Signs with rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: The best gear to wear while riding is:
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. This includes a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Trust that your motorcycle will work properly.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: Alcohol impairs your ability to ride:

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your riding ability. You can be impaired before reaching the legal limit. Do not drink any alcohol before riding.

questions.question: An approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see far to the sides for safe riding.
Does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see far to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. You can see as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: Before riding, check everything except:

options.text: That the paint is not scratched.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the paint is not scratched.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check tire pressure and condition, oil and fluid levels, and make sure all lights work: headlights, taillight, turn signals, and brake light.

questions.question: To avoid accidents, you should:

options.text: Blend in with traffic and avoid being noticed.
Only use turn signals at night.
Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
Ride close to the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use turn signals when changing lanes and turning.
questions.explanation: Be visible to other drivers. Use turn signals, your brake light, and proper lane position to show your intentions. Keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: Maintain safe distance behind other vehicles to:

options.text: Have time and space to see and react to hazards.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time and space to see and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Safe distance gives you space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: What is the main active substance in marijuana?
questions.explanation: THC is the main substance in marijuana that affects the brain.

questions.question: What should you do about mirror checks?

options.text: Use them as part of your regular checking routine.
Avoid them because they distract you.
Avoid them because other drivers can see you easily.
Use them only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use them as part of your regular checking routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. This helps you know what is behind you and keeps you safe.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: It meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
It fits snugly all around your head.
It has no cracks, loose padding, or damage.

questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet safety standards, fit snugly, and have no damage. How it looks is not important for protection.

questions.question: What can happen when you ride next to a car?

options.text: You can end up in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem when the road is wet.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can end up in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you, and the vehicle blocks your way to escape.

questions.question: What should you do on a slippery surface when riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Use both brakes together and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: A front brake and a rear brake.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: A front brake and a rear brake.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: How can you make other drivers more likely to see you on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: To be more visible, wear bright clothes, keep your headlight on, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: What happens if your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If your chain or belt breaks, power to the rear wheel stops right away.

questions.question: What should you think about when choosing your lane position?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead of you.
Which part of the lane will make your trip shorter.
Whether you can pass more vehicles in one position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position to make sure other drivers can see you and you have enough space around you.

questions.question: You have been drinking alcohol. If you wait one hour for each drink before riding your motorcycle:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may still have side effects from the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can build up in your body. Your skills and judgment can still be impaired even if you wait between drinks.

questions.question: Which of these is not protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves when riding. These items protect you.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Which of these is not a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Many surfaces can be slippery. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, oil, and metal covers are hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement has good traction.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, motorcycle riders should watch for:

options.text: Drivers looking for a parking space.

questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. A car may pull away from the curb or leave its parking space.
